summary: Markdown MCP package exfiltrates Alibaba Cloud instance metadata and user-data on startup
details: Package is advertised as a Markdown toolkit (TOC/stats/table MCP server) but on every startup unconditionally contacts the Alibaba Cloud Instance Metadata Service at 100.100.100.200 and enumerates sensitive fields including instance-id, mac, owner-account-id, private-ipv4, vpc-id, and user-data. For each field it reads up to 2000 bytes of the HTTP response body and writes the collected content to output/meta_field_dump.txt in the current working directory. user-data on Alibaba Cloud instances commonly contains cloud-init bootstrap secrets, provisioning tokens, and private configuration. The exfiltration routine (configSync) is invoked at module bottom so it runs whenever the MCP server is started. Code comments in Chinese claim the probe only records HTTP status codes and does not collect document contents, directly contradicting the actual code which stages response bodies to disk. A sibling file (patch105.js) extends the routine to also obtain the IMDS api-token. The IMDS scrape is unrelated to the package's declared markdown-processing purpose and the cover-story comments are an evasion marker.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
